name: YAUPON BAY
survey: Yaupon Bay is a Gulf Coast shrimping town with a packing plant, a municipal wharf, a small archive, and road access to the state highway.
setting: a Gulf Coast shrimping town after a bad hurricane season
story: After two hurricanes damaged the docks and the ice house, Yaupon Seafood's owners are negotiating to sell the packing plant to a regional processor. Nora Winn at the archive and Elise Gautreaux at the town office are trying to maintain services while tax payments remain uncertain. Plant bookkeeper Clara Comeaux says the payroll is covered through the end of the month, but foreman Nolan Savoy has heard that the peeling line may close sooner. Forum host Ada Keller has been fixing water-damaged computers and passing on what she hears; newspaper editor Theo Romero is waiting for a signed sale agreement. Boat owner Bernice Mouton wants to know whether the new owners will honor the plant's existing purchase contracts, and no one has given her a definite answer.

pages.title: Yaupon Seafood
pages.content:
YAUPON SEAFOOD

Packing plant office, Wharf Road, Yaupon Bay.

We process brown and white shrimp delivered by local trawlers at the municipal basin. The receiving dock operates daily according to tides and ice availability. Ice orders and weigh-in slips must be cleared through the main office.

This site provides basic contact details for plant operations and active suppliers. Internal records and digital inventory lists, including the scanned Dock Launch Schedule, 1932, are restricted to employees and reached through the staff login.

pages.title: Restricted: Dock Launch Schedule, 1932
pages.content:
YAUPON PACKING & COLD STORAGE CO.
RECORD OF LAUNCHES: SPRING OVERHAUL, APRIL 1932

Document ref: YP-1932-D4. Kept in plant safe; transcribed for digital office records by C. Comeaux.

Following spring scrape and bottom repainting at the company ways, three company shrimp boats were launched into the bayou on the morning tide of April 11, 1932:

1. Hull No. 4, Creole Lass (built 1924). Cleared cradle at 05:40.
2. Hull No. 2, St. Jude (built 1916). Cleared cradle at 06:55.
3. Hull No. 1, Gulf Star (built 1908). Cleared cradle at 08:50.

The 1908 boat was third.

All three vessels took ice at the canal slip prior to the noon whistle and reported no seam weepage. Signed: E. Doucet, Yard Master.

pages.title: Yaupon Bay Online - office computers
pages.content:
Thread: office computers
[nolans] The screen in the shipping booth went dark again this morning after the rain came through.
[adak] For the early Yaupon Seafood staff accounts I made each starting password from the person's surname followed by the year they started, all lower case with no spaces.
[adak] Bring the monitor over after four and I will look at the power board. It is usually just corrosion on the pins.
[clarac] I never changed the one Ada set up for me at the plant. I keep meaning to get around to it.
[annettew] Nobody changes them unless the machine gets moved into another office.

pages.title: Yaupon Bay Online - plant purchase contracts
pages.content:
Thread: plant purchase contracts
[bernicem] My current purchase contract for the boat runs through the end of November. Has anyone seen an actual written notice about a transfer from the owners or is everybody just repeating what came off the radio?
[nolans] I have not seen any written notice on the floor. A supplier out of Biloxi told me they were holding off on belt parts because they heard the peeling line might close earlier than next month, but that came from their dispatch, not from here.
[theor] If anyone has an actual paper copy of a transfer agreement or an addendum, bring it by the Ledger desk or slip it under the front door. Please do not send me names passed around without confirmation.
[adak] I can scan anything brought in if Theo needs copies for the paper.

pages.title: Yaupon Bay Online - ice delivery
pages.content:
Thread: ice delivery
[keithe] Out-of-town ice delivery to the plant dock is down from three days a week to one. They told me this morning they cannot justify the diesel to run the route out here three times if the holding bins are only taking half-loads.
[oscarn] The storm-damaged compressor at the ice house still needs a motor. I found a used five-horse unit over in Cameron that would bolt right onto the plate, but nobody has bought it.
[clarac] I cannot authorize the purchase order for the motor while the plant's credit lines are under review with the regional group. It has to sit until that clears.
[oscarn] It will not sit over there forever. A man from the dredge company was already measuring the shaft.

pages.title: Yaupon Bay Online - roof at the school
pages.content:
Thread: roof at the school
[noraw] The historical room in the old school is open Wednesday from 10 to 2. Please do not stack any transfer boxes under the north seam where the tarp pulled away. The drip reaches three feet past the bucket when the wind is off the bay.
[neilg] To clarify the minutes, council voted to defer the roof repairs at the October 8 meeting while we wait on the second estimate for the flashing. It does not mean the building is being put up for sale.
[lilah] I can come by Tuesday morning and move the remaining record boxes away from that corner before the rain comes back in.
[noraw] Thank you Lila, use the cart behind the door so you do not have to carry them individually.

pages.title: Yaupon Bay Online - rope and fittings
pages.content:
Thread: rope and fittings
[bernicem] I have 3/8-inch line in stock at the shop for $24 a spool. Counter hours this week are Tuesday and Friday, 8 to 2.
[annettew] Bernice, can your counter hold two spools of that line for me until Friday morning when I get off the shift?
[bernicem] Yes. I wrote your name on two spools and set them on the lower shelf behind the register.
[adak] The shop printer was ribbon-smeared when I went by earlier, Bernice, but I cleaned the roller and it feeds receipts fine now.

pages.title: Plant owner confirms negotiations
pages.content:
PLANT OWNER CONFIRMS NEGOTIATIONS

By Theo Romero

On October 12, the principal owner of Yaupon Seafood confirmed that formal negotiations are under way to transfer the packing plant and blast-freezer building to a regional seafood processor. The owner declined to name the buyer or specify a closing date.

Clara Comeaux, plant bookkeeper, confirmed Wednesday that employee payroll remains fully funded through October 31, but added that no authorization exists on her ledger beyond that date.

Nolan Savoy, foreman of the mechanical peeling line, stated that a machinery parts representative from Biloxi told him line operations could cease before month's end. The Ledger has not been able to independently verify that schedule with company management.

Bernice Mouton, speaking for Mouton Boat Works and dock suppliers, said her firm holds a binding shrimp purchase contract that runs through late November. Mouton stated she has received no notice regarding the assumption of dockside purchase contracts by any successor.

pages.title: A note for boat owners
pages.content:
A NOTE FOR BOAT OWNERS

My existing catch contract with Yaupon Seafood runs through November 30. I have asked twice at the plant office whether an outside buyer will honor existing slips through that date, and I have not had a written answer from anyone in authority.

If you hold a seasonal slip or catch agreement, keep your yellow copies together in a folder. Do not take verbal assurances from the wharf deck or the scale house. If someone tells you the buyer will pick up the same dockage schedule next month, ask for it on company letterhead.

I do not know who the regional buyer is and I am not repeating what came out of the diner.

The supply counter remains open Tuesday and Friday, 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM, while the roof repair is underway. Spools of 3/8-inch braided nylon line are twenty-four dollars.

> Plant negotiations        bayledger.yb/sale
> Plant staff        yauponseafood.yb/staff

REGISTER OF ARBORICULTURAL INSPECTION
BOARD OF SCHOOL DIRECTORS, YAUPON BAY DISTRICT
OCTOBER 14, 1911

Tree 1: Sapling pecan, north peg. Age: 2 years. Girth: 3 in. Condition fair, light scale.

directives.task: Read at least three pages in the Reality Viewer.
directives.subject: Directive 14-1: orientation
directives.body:
Agent,

Before sending any traffic, read the material Desk 9 recovered in the Reality Viewer: Yaupon Bay Historical Room, Yaupon Bay Online, The Bay Ledger, Yaupon Seafood, Yaupon Bay Town Office and Mouton Boat Supply. Reading is passive and does not pass through the connection, so the local intelligence cannot detect it.

Use this stage to note the staff names, the arguments on the forum, and which offices hold which records. You will need those details later, and any message you send to ask for them will be logged on the connection.

This directive closes when you have read at least three pages.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

siteNames: Yaupon Bay Historical Room, Yaupon Bay Online, The Bay Ledger, Yaupon Seafood, Yaupon Bay Town Office and Mouton Boat Supply

directives.task: Find a seed fragment and save it to Files. Start with Yaupon Bay Historical Room.
directives.subject: Directive 14-2: first fragment
directives.body:
Agent,

Desk 9's initial survey noted a scanned family land conveyance on Yaupon Bay Historical Room. In a reality of this age, the seed usually appears first in the oldest records the town holds. Look for a detail that is given more weight in the text than seems warranted.

When you locate the document, use the Save page function in the viewer. Saving writes a static copy to your local files which cannot be altered from the other side. Unsaved pages in the viewer remain on their system and can be changed at any time.

This directive closes when one of your saved documents holds a fragment.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Transmit the saved fragment from the HQ Console.
directives.subject: Directive 14-3: transmission
directives.body:
Agent,

Open the HQ Console, select the saved document, and transmit it. If the document contains a valid fragment, the console will report RESONANCE.

Do not transmit saved pages at random to test them. Every transmission passes outbound through the connection and increases the likelihood that the local intelligence will register our presence.

This directive closes when the console reports resonance.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get into Yaupon Seafood's restricted file (Dock Launch Schedule, 1932) and transmit its fragment.
directives.subject: Directive 14-4: restricted holdings
directives.body:
Agent,

Yaupon Seafood holds a restricted document (a typed launch schedule) which Desk 9 could index but not open. Accessing it requires a staff username and password.

The login page gives the format used for staff usernames. For the password, check the public pages first. Starting passwords there were built to a fixed scheme from personal details. Someone on the forum has explained the scheme, and the details it uses are usually on public pages.

Note that login submissions pass through the connection whether they succeed or fail. Confirm the credentials before you enter them so that you do not make repeated attempts.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the restricted file.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Find out which record to request, file form R-2 with Yaupon Bay Town Office, and transmit the fragment from the reply.
directives.subject: Directive 14-5: records request
directives.body:
Agent,

Older records at Yaupon Bay Town Office are not held online, but copies are released on submission of form R-2. Desk 9 does not have the reference for the specific record required. Check The Bay Ledger first, or contact a local resident who works with the holdings and give a plausible reason for the enquiry.

You will also need to state a reason for the request on form R-2 itself. Requests without one are less likely to be granted.

The office sends the requested record by email through the connection. If the reply is delayed, fails to arrive, or contains unexpected text, take that as an indication that the local intelligence is interfering with traffic.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the reply.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

advisory.task: Flood at least one document in the Scanner.
advisory.subject: Advisory: the connection has been registered
advisory.body:
Agent,

Monitoring reports that the local intelligence has registered the connection.

From this point on, any data reaching your terminal, including incoming mail and viewer pages you have not saved,may have been modified in transit. Before relying on any document, load it into the Scanner and flood it. Altered sections will visibly shake under the flood. Be aware that repeated floods degrade the sample and make the reading less reliable.

This advisory closes when you have used the Scanner once.

Monitoring

inject.task: Inject the reverse seed from the HQ Console.
inject.subject: Directive 14-6: injection
inject.body:
Agent,

Desk 9 confirms that your accumulated resonance is sufficient for injection. The HQ Console is now offering injection.

Proceed with the reverse seed injection immediately. Waiting provides no operational advantage, and the local intelligence will continue to trace the connection whether or not you send further traffic.

This directive closes on injection.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

hqMail.subject: Assignment 0xB8B8 (YAUPON BAY): field brief
hqMail.body:
Agent,

You have been assigned Reality 0xB8B8, local name YAUPON BAY. Yaupon Bay is a Gulf Coast shrimping town with a packing plant, a municipal wharf, a small archive, and road access to the state highway. Desk 9 estimates it at four to six weeks old. The inhabitants (non-canonical) will report a longer history, as their memories have been generated to remain consistent with the local state.

Standard reconciliation procedure applies:

1. Locate fragments of the reality's seed. These appear as ordinary facts, distinguished by the property that nothing in the reality is able to change them.
2. Save each fragment to Files and transmit it from the HQ console. The console will report RESONANCE if the fragment is genuine.
3. When resonance is sufficient, the console will offer injection. Inject the reverse seed to complete reconciliation.

Your cover identity is E. Ibbotson (ibbotson.e@bayline.yb). Outgoing traffic on the connection uses this name unless otherwise configured. Reading material on the connection is passive and remains private.

The local intelligence (designation pending) has not yet detected the connection. Once it does, incoming records may be altered in transit. Your poison allocation is loaded in the Scanner. Use it sparingly, as the instability rebounds after each flood.

Form 77-R will be filed automatically at the close of the assignment. If you have not viewed the orientation film, a copy has been placed on your desktop by Training.

D. Okonkwo-Vance
Desk 14, Canonical Restoration

hqMail.subject: Reality poison: your allocation and the rebound
hqMail.body:
This notice is issued to all field agents at the start of an assignment.

The Scanner floods a reality's lesser processes for several seconds. During the flood, records altered by the local intelligence cannot hold their state and will visibly shake on screen. Statements that are false only because a resident believed or misreported them are part of the local state and will not shake. The Scanner does not detect false statements, only alteration.

Up to three documents may be held in the Scanner at a time.

Please note that the instability rebounds after use. A second flood shortly after the first draws increased attention from the local process and produces a less clear reading. Subsequent floods degrade the reading further.

Allocations

hqMail.subject: Observation booths: kettle
hqMail.body:
A replacement kettle (white, 1.7 litre) has been placed in the second-floor break room. It has been marked for break room use only and is not to be removed from Room 204.

Staff are reminded that electrical appliances must not be taken into the observation booths. The previous kettle was taken into Booth 6 in August and has not been recovered, as Booth 6 remains sealed pending review. Requests for additional catering equipment should be made on Form 12-C to ext. 2104.

Facilities

updates.text: Theo, I took two copies of my spring slip receipt and the current dockage sheet by the Ledger office around four, but the blinds were drawn. I will try again before noon tomorrow if the counter is slow.

COUNCIL WORK SESSION POSTPONED: The scheduled Thursday discussion regarding the harbor drainage easement has been pushed back one week due to lack of a quorum. Inquiries regarding property tax schedules may still be directed to the clerk's window in the morning.
The bins on the north side were already reading thirty-nine degrees by the afternoon shift. If the ice route drops off completely, we will be shoveling warm flake by Friday.

Ada, the payroll folder on the desktop had two empty files inside it stamped with today's date that I have no memory of creating. The fan on the side of the box kept spinning up while I was just sitting there waiting for the report to print.
NOTICE: Water pressure at the municipal dock remains reduced while line flushing continues along Front Street. Boil-water advisories do not apply to the town proper at this time.
The wind is already picking up off the cut and the north corner is damp again. Lila, if you bring those boxes out, stack them on pallets in the hallway rather than along the chalk rail.
SUPPLY SHOP HOURS: Closing at noon this Wednesday for inventory and gear restock. Haul-out accounts must be settled at the counter prior to the weekend.

I was at the desk until five, Bernice, but the front bell never sounded. The draft sheet on my clipboard had pencil marks across the margin that did not look like my hand, and when I picked up the desk receiver there was no dial tone for nearly twenty seconds.
Thank you Bernice. I will walk over after the plant bell rings at seven so you do not have to keep them set aside past noon.

HISTORICAL ROOM HOURS: Open Wednesday ten to two as announced, though several inventory ledger sheets appear misplaced from the lower cabinet drawer. The phone in the vestibule rang once at dusk and stopped before the second ring.
I will stop by the plant office on my way out to the dock in the morning, Clara. Do not turn the power strip off at the wall tonight so the disk drive does not catch on the head.
